reports.title: Jos Tartese-Joy: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: I note that it was found that there was no nationally recognised way of flagging in maternity notes that a pregnancy is considered high-risk. As a consequence, the community midwife and GP were not aware that the pregnancy was high-risk, and additionally the mother herself was not explicitly counselled about this.
promises.summary: Introduce nationally recognised flagging for high-risk pregnancies in maternity notes

concerns.quote: no nationally recognised way of flagging this within the notes
concerns.hazard: lack of flagging high risk pregnancy

concerns.quote: no plan for an induction of labour in place
concerns.hazard: no induction plan for high risk pregnancy

concerns.quote: layout of maternity services at the trust meant that triage and delivery were on different floors
concerns.hazard: separate floors for triage and delivery

concerns.quote: CTG monitoring should have | taken place at admission
concerns.hazard: lack of admission CTG monitoring for high risk pregnancy

concerns.quote: lack of clarity regarding the escalation process she needed to follow
concerns.hazard: unclear escalation process for trainee midwife

concerns.quote: guidance nationally was not to look at this but to look at the % weight _ change

reports.title: Esme Atkinson: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: The inquest heard evidence that health visitors /midwives and GPs play a key role in the early identification of a heart defect such as Esme's at an early stage. Such a defect will rarely be apparent at the 72 hour check on the evidence given at the inquest but symptoms will manifest subsequently. Such symptoms can be subtle and the inquest was told that for there to be early suspicion, of a heart defect, training for community midwives/health visitors and GPs needed to be improved and good quality information sharing was also essential. This should include concerns around feeding and weight loss.
concerns.hazard: delayed detection of congenital heart defect

concerns.quote: The GP check at 6- 8 weeks was a key checking point but needed to be informed by asking all of the right questions and a good understanding of how to listen for such a heart defect.
concerns.hazard: missed opportunity for congenital heart defect detection at 6-8 week GP visit

concerns.quote: The inquest was told that it was important that it was understood by health professionals involved in the care of a baby that the mother being diabetic increased the risk of a defect significantly and should increase the care taken in relation to presenting symptoms.
concerns.hazard: inadequate risk assessment for infants of diabetic mothers

concerns.quote: There was no routine echocardiogram of a baby born of a mother with diabetes nationally although their risk of a defect was significantly higher than other babies and such a test it would detect a baby with a ventricular septal defect at an early stage
concerns.hazard: absence of national protocol for routine echocardiography in infants of diabetic mothers

concerns.quote: In Esme's case although her mum's identical twin had a heart defect this did not in the North West, trigger the protocol for a routine echocardiogram. A heart defect in her mother would have. It was unclear why this was excluded given the genetic link.
concerns.hazard: failure to apply genetic risk protocol for family history of congenital heart defect

concerns.quote: The evidence of the paediatricians at the inquest was that tracking weight on the centile chart even from an early point assisted in understanding if there was a significant issue in relation to feeding triggering professional curiosity. However the evidence from the Health Visitor appeared to suggest that centile tracking was not seen as useful before 1 month and the red book was not used to look at weight centile tracking in the early stages.
concerns.hazard: delayed recognition of feeding and weight issues as warning signs

links.explanation: Both reports concern the use of infant weight monitoring via centile charts and the interpretation of weight changes.
links.earlier_quote: guidance nationally was not to look at this but to look at the % weight _ change between the last weight and the new weight.
links.later_quote: tracking weight on the centile chart even from an early point assisted in understanding if there was a significant issue in relation to feeding triggering professional curiosity.
